parsed.rationale: The structural evidence shows `shared_field_count: 16` with `differing_slots: null`, meaning all three type-alias-union declarations are bit-for-bit identical in shape. All three records share `package: "Wallpaper"` and reside in `Shared/Wallpaper/Sources/Wallpaper/Core/`, so no cross-package boundary is involved. The three names (`PlaybackBlendMode`, `MaterialBlendMode`, `OverlayBlendMode`) suggest the same underlying blend-mode union is being re-declared once per usage context rather than shared. Maintaining three identical 16-case union definitions in the same package creates a silent divergence risk: a future case addition must be applied in three places. Unifying to one canonical declaration with optional typealiases eliminates that risk without breaking existing call-sites.

specifics.proposed_action: Consolidate the three identical type-alias-union declarations — `PlaybackBlendMode` (PlaybackBlendMode.swift, line 21), `MaterialBlendMode` (MaterialBlendMode.swift, line 21), and `OverlayBlendMode` (_Plant_OverlayBlendMode.swift, line 21) — into a single canonical type declaration inside the `Wallpaper` package (e.g., `Shared/Wallpaper/Sources/Wallpaper/Core/BlendMode.swift`). Each of the three names can then be preserved as a `typealias` pointing to the single canonical type if source compatibility is required, or call-sites can be migrated to the canonical name and the aliases removed entirely.
specifics.why_no_category_fits: All three records are `type-alias-union` kinds, not structs, classes, or free functions, so `generic-parameterization` and `subclass-lift` do not apply. They are not protocols, so `protocol-inheritance`, `default-implementation`, and `pat-introduction` do not apply. They all live in the same package (`Wallpaper`), so `extract-to-common` (which requires moving to an upstream package that multiple consumer packages already depend on) is not the right framing — no cross-package extraction is needed. The duplication is a straightforward same-package triplication of an identical 16-field union type under three different names; the correct fix is to unify the declaration in place and optionally retain typealiases for the distinct semantic names, which is an intra-package deduplication action that none of the named categories precisely describe.
